groups.label: The operating system itself
groups.blurb: The parts that keep the rest of it running, indexed, healthy and honest.

modules.name: santa
modules.label: Autonomy Policy
modules.tagline: Declare what an automated run may touch, then read the policy back.
modules.description: You write four files: which projects an automated run may touch, which capabilities are allowed at all, whether web and outbound message actions are approved, and whether the whole thing is in dry run. It reads those back and reports which of the actions you declared pass your own filters. It runs none of them, and it ships with the policy empty on purpose.
canDo: List the candidate actions you declared that pass your own policy
Show which projects and capabilities are currently in scope
Report the state of the web and outbound message approval gates
Confirm whether the whole thing is still in dry run
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline. You fill in the policy files yourself.

modules.name: doctor
modules.label: Doctor
modules.tagline: Check whether your install is actually healthy, then fix two of the faults.
modules.description: It runs five read-only checks on your own install: is the app serving, are your modules intact, is the automation hook registered, is the search index fresh, and are any installs broken. Two of those findings it can put right, by re-running an installer you already listed in your config or rebuilding a stale index. Nothing else gets touched.
canDo: Check whether your app is serving on the address you configured
Verify every installed module still has the files it installed
Confirm the automation hook is registered in your settings file
Report whether the search index exists and how stale it is
Rebuild a missing or stale index using your own rebuild command
Re-run the installer for a module that came back broken
modules.needs: Nothing, it reads your own install once you fill in the paths

modules.name: evolver
modules.label: Evolver
modules.tagline: Notices what you keep repeating and proposes a fix you have to approve.
modules.description: Evolver watches how you actually work on this machine, spots the same request coming round again, and writes it up as a proposal: a shortcut, a repair, a route worth making permanent. Watching is off until you switch it on, everything stays in a locked folder on your own machine, and nothing is applied until you approve it by token. Its own safety rules cannot be edited by a proposal.
canDo: Record what you ask for and find the patterns that repeat
Surface recurring failures and gaps worth fixing
Draft a bounded repair or a shortcut for a weekly routine
Hold every proposal until you approve it by token
Report exactly what it can and cannot do right now
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline

modules.name: ontology
modules.label: Identity Ontology
modules.tagline: A starter identity map so one person is not three separate records.
modules.description: The ontology names your records, the stores that hold them, and the safe rules for joining them. It ships one worked example: resolve a contact across a CRM and an address book by matching normalised email first, then phone. It is a small teaching scaffold with synthetic demo data, meant to be replaced with your own entities and rules.
canDo: Resolve a contact across your identity stores
Match on normalised email first, then normalised phone
Describe entities, stores and join rules in one registry
Try the resolver against synthetic demo data before wiring real records
Extend the schema with your own entities and stores
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline

modules.name: mac-cleaner
modules.label: Mac Cleaner
modules.tagline: Finds what is eating your disk, and removes nothing until you confirm.
modules.description: Mac Cleaner looks only inside the folders you list in its config, and that config ships empty, so a fresh install cannot see any of your files. It reports exact paths and sizes, and applies the backup retention rules you set. Removal takes a second run carrying the confirmation token, and every file is rechecked in the moment before it goes. Deletion is permanent.
canDo: Audit the folders you configured and show what is taking up space
Preview the old files a cleanup would remove
Delete those files once you pass the confirmation token
Preview which backup archives your retention rules would drop
Prune old backup archives after you confirm
modules.needs: A config listing the folders it may look at. No account needed.

modules.name: mission-control-core
modules.label: Mission Control
modules.tagline: The workspace the rest of All Sorted plugs into.
modules.description: A local app that runs on your own machine: a dashboard, a task board, projects, a calendar view, settings, and a page showing which modules you have installed. It ships as the core, and modules such as the CRM add their own pages on top of it. Your notes and files stay in a workspace folder you control.
canDo: Run a dashboard, task board and project notes on your own machine
See which All Sorted modules are installed and what state they are in
Keep working notes and decisions in a workspace folder you own
Take module pages, such as the CRM, as overlays on the same app
Back up workspace data with credential files kept out of the archive
modules.needs: Node.js on your own machine, nothing else to start

modules.name: organizer
modules.label: Organizer
modules.tagline: Keep an index of every recipe, skill, and workflow on your machine.
modules.description: It walks a directory you point it at, finds every recipe, skill, workflow, and project file, and writes them into a local index that the routing system reads. It also tells you whether that index has gone stale, and finds dead links or orphan entries inside it. Everything stays on your machine, and no source file it reads is ever rewritten.
canDo: Index a directory of recipes, skills, workflows, and projects
Check whether the index is stale before paying for a full rebuild
Audit the index for dead links and orphan entries
Confirm the machine is ready to index
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline

modules.name: overseer
modules.label: Overseer
modules.tagline: Tells you when something you run has stopped, filled up, or gone stale.
modules.description: Six checks over the things you configure: services and processes, scheduled jobs, free disk space, log directory size, backup freshness, and env file syntax. All six only read. Two repairs can act, restarting a service you listed and clearing a lock once it is genuinely stale. Both run straight away, and both only touch entries you put in the config yourself.
canDo: Check whether your configured services and processes are still alive
Check whether scheduled jobs have reported in recently
Watch free disk space and log directory size against your own limits
Check backups are recent and env files are not malformed
Restart a stopped service you listed, then verify it came back
Clear a lock file once it is past the stale window you set
modules.needs: A config listing the services, jobs, paths and locks you want watched

modules.name: parallel-sidecars
modules.label: Parallel Sidecars
modules.tagline: Works out which parts of a job can run in the background at once.
modules.description: Before a long job starts, this decides which parts can run beside the main thread, how many lanes there should be, and what each one is allowed to touch. It plans only: it never launches a worker and never edits your files. Writable lanes are off by default, and when you turn them on they work in a disposable copy of the repository and hand back a patch to read.
canDo: Plan which parts of a job can run in parallel
Cap how many lanes run and how much each one may touch
See the exact gate that held a writable lane back
Inspect what a sidecar patch would change before anything is applied
Check what this install is currently allowed to do
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline. Git on your PATH for writable lanes

modules.name: report-relay
modules.label: Report Relay
modules.tagline: Formats a status report and shows you exactly what would be sent.
modules.description: Report Relay turns a title, a summary and a priority into a consistently formatted status report, then previews where that report would go. The recipes format and preview only: nothing is delivered to Telegram or anywhere else from here. It states plainly whether a destination is configured, so a preview is never mistaken for a send.
canDo: Format a title, summary and priority into a clean report
Keep the priority honest instead of marking everything urgent
Preview the delivery destination before anything goes out
Confirm whether a Telegram destination is actually configured
Keep bot tokens and chat IDs out of the output
modules.needs: Nothing to format a report. Your own Telegram bot token and chat ID to preview a real destination

modules.name: skills
modules.label: Skills Pack
modules.tagline: Twenty ready-made skills for planning, debugging, writing, and reviewing.
modules.description: Twenty skills that need no keys and no setup: twelve written for All Sorted, and eight third-party MIT skills that ship with their original licences and credit. They cover planning before you build, debugging to root cause, verifying a change, and getting the AI smell out of your writing. Two of them, CRM and Form Builder, need their matching app modules.
canDo: Plan a change properly before any code gets written
Debug a failure to root cause instead of guessing at a fix
Verify a change actually works before calling it done
Strip AI writing patterns out of a draft and put your voice back
Review a diff with a fresh set of eyes
Check a site for broken links or a service for uptime
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline

modules.name: strategist
modules.label: Strategist
modules.tagline: One short brief each morning on the three things that actually matter.
modules.description: You describe your business once, drop in notes as things happen, and it produces a daily brief: three ranked priorities, what is at risk, where the money is, and an honest line on whether you are drifting. Seven strategy lenses argue it out first, and disagreement is kept rather than averaged away. It is an advisor: it sends nothing and moves no money.
canDo: Produce a daily brief with three ranked priorities
Run a weekly portfolio review instead of the daily brief
Check mid-day whether what you are doing matches today's priorities
Read the last three briefs so priorities cannot quietly roll forward
Write out the full prompt when the local Claude tool is not installed
modules.needs: Node.js and Claude Code on your own machine, under your own login

groups.label: Clients, sales and money
groups.blurb: Who is in your pipeline, what they owe you, and what the books say.

modules.name: apollo
modules.label: Apollo
modules.tagline: Look up companies and people for sales research, using your own Apollo account.
modules.description: Apollo is where you check a company or a contact before you go after them. It searches for people and companies, and fills in a record when you already have an email address or a domain. It runs on your own Apollo key, spends your credits, and reports only what Apollo actually returned. If a field comes back empty, it says so rather than guessing.
canDo: Search for companies by industry, size, or location
Find the people at a target company by role
Fill in a contact record from an email address
Fill in a company record from a domain
Check your key is set up before you spend any credits
modules.needs: Your own Apollo API key. There is a credential-free demo without one.

modules.name: bookkeeper
modules.label: Bookkeeper
modules.tagline: Imports your statements, sorts the entries, and holds back the doubtful ones.
modules.description: Bookkeeper reads bank statements as CSV, OFX, QIF or PDF, builds balanced double entry journals, and puts anything it is not confident about into a review queue with the reason. It runs on your machine and takes no bank login. Nothing reaches your ledger until you have seen the diff and confirmed it. It reports on money, it never moves it.
canDo: Import statements as CSV, OFX, QIF or PDF
Pull vendor, date, totals and line items off an invoice or receipt
Sort transactions into accounts and flag the uncertain ones
Work a review queue, and turn your corrections into rules
Post balanced journals once you confirm the diff
Run profit and loss, cash position and ageing reports
modules.needs: Your own statement files. No bank login, no credentials

modules.name: crm
modules.label: CRM
modules.tagline: A contact and pipeline workspace that lives in your own Mission Control.
modules.description: Contacts, a pipeline board, activity history, labels and saved views, all held in a local database on your machine. Automation rules can draft follow-up messages from your own templates, but every one lands in an approval queue first. Live sending stays off until you add your own credentials and switch the channel on.
canDo: Keep contacts, notes and activity history in one place
Move leads through pipeline stages on a board
Group people with labels and saved views
Draft follow-up messages from your own templates
Hold every automated message in an approval queue before delivery
Track affiliates and their payouts
modules.needs: A Mission Control install, plus your own email credentials if you want to send

modules.name: kajabi
modules.label: Kajabi
modules.tagline: Runs contacts, tags, offers, and orders inside your own Kajabi site.
modules.description: This connects to your Kajabi site through its API. It reads contacts, courses, offers, orders, and payouts, so you can answer a question without logging in. Anything that changes a student's record, their access, or their subscription shows you the plan first and waits for your approval. It does not email students, and it does not publish or edit course content.
canDo: Find a contact and see what they bought
List your courses, offers, orders, and payouts
Add a contact, a tag, or a note once you approve it
Grant or revoke access to an offer, record by record
Cancel, pause, or reactivate a purchase after you confirm
Set up or remove an API webhook
modules.needs: Your own Kajabi client ID and secret

modules.name: lusha
modules.label: Lusha
modules.tagline: Looks up business contact details for one named person at a time.
modules.description: Lusha connects to your own Lusha account and finds a business contact you can already name, by email, full name or LinkedIn URL. One person per request: there is no batch, CSV or list import, and it refuses anything shaped like a bulk export. Results are not stored, logged or cached by the module.
canDo: Search for one named business contact
Reveal emails or phone numbers for a contact you have confirmed
Find a phone number in one step, search then reveal
Check how many account credits you have left
Refuse bulk or list shaped requests before they reach the API
modules.needs: Your own Lusha account and API key

modules.name: stripe
modules.label: Stripe
modules.tagline: Answers revenue questions and sets up checkout without five dashboards.
modules.description: Stripe reads the account you connect: balance, revenue over a date range, payment links and promotion codes. Creating a payment link or a promo code starts as a plan and only runs when you type the exact confirmation phrase. Refunds, direct charges and subscription changes are not built into it, so it cannot move your money.
canDo: Summarise available and pending balance
Summarise revenue over a chosen number of days
List existing payment links and promotion codes
Plan a payment link, then create it on your confirmation
Plan a promo code, then create it on your confirmation
Verify a new promo code at live checkout before you share the link
modules.needs: Your own Stripe secret key

modules.name: zoho-books
modules.label: Zoho Books
modules.tagline: Read your books and raise invoices, bills and expenses in your own Zoho.
modules.description: It talks to your own Zoho Books organisation with your own credentials. Most of it reads: invoices, bills, expenses, contacts, items, bank accounts and transactions, payments in and out, the chart of accounts and the dashboard. Creating an invoice, contact or expense, pushing journals, and sending an invoice are the write actions, and each one needs your say-so.
canDo: List and open invoices, bills, expenses and payments
Pull the chart of accounts, bank accounts and bank transactions
Read contacts, items and your organisation settings
See the accounting dashboard at a glance
Create an invoice, contact or expense, and push validated journal entries
Send an invoice to a customer, on your confirmation
modules.needs: Your own Zoho OAuth client, refresh token and organisation ID

groups.label: Inbox, messaging and meetings
groups.blurb: The channels that eat your day, handled with drafts you approve.

modules.name: calendar-brief-mcp
modules.label: Calendar Brief
modules.tagline: Turn your calendar into a daily brief, open windows, and meeting prep.
modules.description: It reads your own calendar through a connection you configure and tells you what the day looks like: what is busy, what clashes, where the gaps are, and what you need to know before the next call. It can also add, move, and cancel events on your own calendar. It refuses outright if you try to add attendees, because inviting someone is a message to a real person.
canDo: Build a daily brief with conflicts and free time
Find open windows today, tomorrow, or across the week
Prep you for a meeting with attendees, links, and nearby context
Add an event to your own calendar without double booking on a retry
Move or retitle an event and report exactly what changed
Cancel an event on your own calendar
modules.needs: Your own calendar account, connected through a command you configure

modules.name: teddy
modules.label: Chat Cleanup
modules.tagline: Turn a chat export into a cleanup list you review yourself.
modules.description: You give it an export of your conversations and a retention window. It flags two things: threads that are nothing but automated notifications, and threads with no activity since your cut off. Everything comes back as a plan you can read or save to a file. It never logs into an account and deletes nothing, because it has no connection to delete through.
canDo: Flag conversations with no activity past your retention window
Flag threads that carry only automated or service messages
Preview the full review list before you touch anything
Save the plan to a file for review or approval
Set and check the retention window it works to
modules.needs: A conversation export you provide. No account login.

modules.name: email-agent
modules.label: Email Agent
modules.tagline: Triage your inbox and write replies you send yourself.
modules.description: It reads a message you give it, sorts it against your own keywords and sender rules, and suggests review or a label. It writes reply drafts that stay on your machine. It never sends, never auto-replies, and never changes your mailbox: the sending happens in your own mail client, by you.
canDo: Triage a message into a review or label suggestion
Draft a reply for you to review and send yourself
Sort against your own urgent keywords and sender rules
Check whether your mailbox connector is configured
modules.needs: Nothing to start. Your own Google OAuth connector only if you want it reading a live mailbox

modules.name: postmaster-tools
modules.label: Postmaster Tools
modules.tagline: See how Gmail treats the mail going out from your sending domain.
modules.description: It reads Google Postmaster Tools for a domain your own Google account already has in there: spam rate, SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass rates, delivery errors, and outbound TLS. It can register a new domain for tracking, but it cannot verify one, that is a DNS record you add yourself at Google. Every number comes back with the window it covers.
canDo: Check your domain's Gmail spam rate
Check SPF, DKIM, and DMARC pass rates
Check the delivery error rate and outbound TLS encryption rate
Pull a full deliverability and reputation report for a domain
Register a new sending domain for tracking
Re-check whether Google now lists a domain you registered
modules.needs: Your own Google OAuth client ID, secret, and refresh token

modules.name: resend
modules.label: Resend
modules.tagline: Drafts a transactional email and sends it only when you say go.
modules.description: This sends email through your own Resend account. Ask it to send and it comes back with the full draft first: recipient, sender, subject, body. Nothing reaches an inbox until you confirm that exact message, every time. It also tells you which of your sending domains are verified, and whether an earlier email arrived. Single sends, not bulk lists.
canDo: Draft an email and show you exactly what would go out
Send it once you confirm that specific message
List the domains you are verified to send from
Check whether an earlier email was delivered
Test that the connection to your account is live
modules.needs: Your own Resend API key

modules.name: slack
modules.label: Slack
modules.tagline: Read your Slack workspace, and post only when you confirm it.
modules.description: It lists channels, reads channel history, searches messages, and checks which identity your token belongs to. It can post a channel message or a direct message, but both default to a preview: you see the exact text and the target, and nothing is sent until you confirm that specific message. A previous yes never carries over to the next one.
canDo: List the channels your token can see
Read recent messages in a channel
Search message history across your workspace
Check which identity the connected token belongs to
Draft a channel message or a direct message and preview it first
Post that message only after you confirm it
modules.needs: Your own Slack bot token, plus a user token for search

modules.name: ai-agent-income-telegram-gate
modules.label: Telegram Access Gate
modules.tagline: Paid members get into your Telegram group, lapsed ones get removed.
modules.description: It binds your checkout links to Telegram accounts, issues a single-use invite once a subscription is active, and removes members after a subscription lapses. It runs against your own Telegram bot and your own Supabase billing records. Removal never happens on a first run: reconcile shows you who would go, and acts only when you confirm.
canDo: Issue a one-time group invite when a subscription is active
Remove a member when their subscription is deleted or lapses
Preview a full reconcile before anyone is removed
Refuse a run that would empty the group or that reads an empty billing source
Report which configuration values are set without printing them
modules.needs: Your Telegram bot token, group ID, Supabase keys, and a webhook secret

modules.name: whatsapp
modules.label: WhatsApp
modules.tagline: Links a WhatsApp account you own, and tells you if it is still connected.
modules.description: This pairs a WhatsApp account you own with a local server on your machine, by QR code or pairing code. The recipe it ships is a read-only status check: not linked, linked but offline, or connected. Checking never sends anything and never triggers a reconnect. Sending is a separate command that refuses to run without an explicit send confirmation, every time.
canDo: Pair a WhatsApp account you own by QR or pairing code
Check whether it is unlinked, offline, or connected
List the contacts held in the local session
Send a message only when you pass the explicit send confirmation
Unlink the local session, behind its own confirmation
modules.needs: A WhatsApp account you own, a phone to scan with, and Node 22

modules.name: zoom
modules.label: Zoom
modules.tagline: Handles meeting admission and recording retention, never the content.
modules.description: Zoom connects to your own account with server to server OAuth credentials. It counts cloud recording sets for a date range, queues local recordings by filename, and sets waiting room and join before host on a meeting. It never downloads, transcribes or exports what was said. Deleting old cloud recordings needs a confirmation token matching the previewed count.
canDo: Count cloud recording sets for a date range
Queue local recordings by filename only
Set waiting room and join before host on a meeting
Verify a meeting's admission settings
Preview which cloud recordings a retention cutoff would delete
Delete them once you supply the matching confirmation token
modules.needs: Your own Zoom server to server OAuth credentials

groups.label: Content and brand
groups.blurb: Writing, decks, proof and posts, in your voice rather than a generic one.

modules.name: branding-manager
modules.label: Branding Manager
modules.tagline: Keeps a written brand brain per project, and checks your copy against it.
modules.description: Branding Manager builds a living brand file for each project you register: who you speak to, how you sound, what you are allowed to claim. Then it scores drafts against the right brand, tracks drift across weeks rather than one snapshot, and audits a funnel for the point where the story stops holding. It runs on your machine with no API key.
canDo: Set up a brand brain for a new project
Score a draft against the right brand, with the evidence shown
Check recent content for brand drift, and trend it over time
Compare two brands when they start sounding the same
Run a guided positioning workshop, one exercise at a time
Audit a funnel against the brand positioning
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline

modules.name: instagram
modules.label: Instagram
modules.tagline: Reads your account, drafts the post, and publishes only when you confirm.
modules.description: Instagram connects to your own account, through the official Meta Graph API when you provide those credentials, or through an unofficial fallback when you do not. It reads account and post statistics, reads comments on your own posts, and drafts feed images, carousels and reels. Publishing, replying and direct messages are irreversible, so each one needs the word PUBLISH for that exact request.
canDo: Read account and recent media statistics
Read comments on your own posts and reels
Draft a feed image, a carousel of 2 to 10 images, or a reel
Publish a post, reel or story once you confirm with PUBLISH
Reply to a comment after the same confirmation
Send a direct message after the same confirmation, on the fallback transport only
modules.needs: Your own Meta Graph API credentials, or an Instagram login for the unofficial fallback, which may breach Instagram's terms

modules.name: postpilot
modules.label: PostPilot
modules.tagline: Research, draft and SEO-shape a blog post, then publish only when you say.
modules.description: It researches a topic, outlines it, writes a draft, scores readability and keyword density, works out a slug and schema, and stages the result on your machine. That is the whole automatic part. Publishing to WordPress, Ghost or a markdown file is one separate command with an explicit confirm flag, and there is no scheduler that could run it for you.
canDo: Suggest blog topics from your business and content pillars
Research, outline and write a draft from a brief you supply
Score readability and keyword density, and write meta title and description
Stage drafts locally and list what is waiting
Publish to WordPress, Ghost or markdown, only on an explicit confirmation
modules.needs: Nothing to draft. Your own CMS details only when you want to publish

modules.name: vsl-agent
modules.label: Sales Video Planner
modules.tagline: Plans a sales video from your brief. You still write the script.
modules.description: It turns your brief into an ordered beat sheet: hook, stakes, mechanism, demonstration, proof, objections, offer and terms, call to action. Every beat carries your own material, and any beat you have not supplied the material for is marked blocked rather than filled in with invention. It checks the material terms are stated before the ask.
canDo: Outline the beats of a sales video from your own brief
Mark every beat you have not supplied the material for
Check price, billing, delivery, guarantee and eligibility are stated before the ask
Scan a draft for the ten kinds of statement that need evidence or sign-off
Critique a draft against the beat and scene standard
Show a worked example plan from an invented brief
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline

modules.name: slide-deck-builder
modules.label: Slide Deck Builder
modules.tagline: Turns a goal into a deck that argues something, then builds it.
modules.description: It drafts the five beat story first, turns your brief into an outline, and renders a self contained HTML deck that opens without a network connection. The build fails on craft and layout breaks rather than shipping six bullets and no point of view. It can also create the deck in your own Google Slides account, and it never shares or emails it.
canDo: Draft a five beat narrative arc before writing a single slide
Turn a goal or brief into a deck outline
Build a self contained HTML deck that opens offline
Fail the build on bullet count, headline length and layout breaks
Critique a finished deck against the craft rules
Create the deck in your own Google Slides account
modules.needs: Nothing for local decks. Your own Google service account for the Slides export

modules.name: testimonial-selector
modules.label: Testimonial Selector
modules.tagline: Ranks the customer quotes you already hold and shows what they do not prove.
modules.description: It reads your approved quotes, ranks them against a chosen audience, and explains every placing: measured results, timeframes, before and after, the speaker's role, answered doubts, and the vague praise it marks down. It also checks a quote for the problems that would stop you publishing it, and reports which of your claims no approved quote backs up.
canDo: Rank your approved quotes for a specific audience
Explain in plain words why each quote placed where it did
Flag wording that needs sign-off, such as earnings, health or absolute claims
Catch the record problems people forget: no attribution, no consent, no capture date
Report which of your claims have no approved quote behind them
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline

groups.label: Marketing and search
groups.blurb: Getting found, staying found, and following up without nagging.

modules.name: backlinks
modules.label: Backlinks
modules.tagline: Find backlink prospects, watch the links you have, and draft the outreach.
modules.description: It looks for link opportunities using your own Ahrefs, SerpAPI and Hunter.io keys, then checks every placement you have registered with a real request to see whether your link is still on the page. It can write an outreach email for a prospect it found. It never sends it. That part stays with you.
canDo: Find link prospects from competitor gaps and search footprints
Track every placement you register and flag links that have gone
Look up a contact for a prospect domain when Hunter.io is configured
Draft an outreach email for a prospect it actually found
Report prospects and live placements by Domain Rating
Run an offline demo before you add any keys
modules.needs: Optional Ahrefs, SerpAPI and Hunter.io keys. Link tracking needs none.

modules.name: dittofeed
modules.label: Dittofeed
modules.tagline: Runs the lifecycle email automations on a Dittofeed you host yourself.
modules.description: This connects to a Dittofeed deployment you run and own. It updates customer profiles, records lifecycle events, tells you what is sitting in the local send queue, and retries anything stuck. It lists your journeys, reads the email copy inside them, and pauses or resumes one only when you name the journey and confirm. It never sends a campaign or a test email itself.
canDo: Update a customer profile or record a lifecycle event
Check what is waiting in the local send queue
Retry the events that got stuck
List your automation journeys and see which are running
Read the email copy a journey actually sends
Pause or resume a journey after you confirm it
modules.needs: Your own Dittofeed deployment, plus its write and admin keys

modules.name: meta-ads
modules.label: Meta Ads
modules.tagline: Read your Facebook and Instagram ad numbers, and pause or resume a campaign.
modules.description: It pulls campaigns, ad sets, ads, and insights from your own Meta ad account so you can see what is spending and what is working. It can pause or activate a campaign, but only after you confirm that exact campaign by name and ID. It cannot change budgets, build campaigns, or edit creative. Without credentials it stays offline and only checks readiness.
canDo: List the campaigns, ad sets, and ads on your account
Pull account and campaign insights for a date range you choose
Show a dashboard of how the ad account is doing
Pause a live campaign after you confirm that exact campaign
Activate a paused campaign after you confirm that exact campaign
Check whether your ad account is connected yet
modules.needs: Your own Meta access token and ad account ID

modules.name: seo
modules.label: SEO Agent
modules.tagline: Audit a page, build a content brief, and write a draft for review.
modules.description: It fetches a public page and checks the on-page basics: title, description, H1, canonical link, image alt text, HTTP status. It turns a target keyword into a structured brief with an outline and FAQs, then turns that brief into a Markdown draft. There is no publishing command, no rank tracking, and no Search Console writes: nothing it produces reaches a live site.
canDo: Audit a public page for on-page issues
Turn a target keyword into a brief with an outline and FAQs
Write a review-only Markdown draft from that brief
Report which optional search providers are configured
modules.needs: Nothing, the audit, brief and draft all run without an API key

modules.name: seo-monitor
modules.label: SEO Monitor
modules.tagline: Audits the public SEO signals on a page and says what is missing.
modules.description: SEO Monitor fetches a public page and reports the title, meta description, canonical tag, robots.txt and sitemap.xml as they actually are, not as they should be. Core Web Vitals come from Google's public PageSpeed API when you add your own key. It reads only: it cannot change a page and it does not log into Search Console.
canDo: Audit a public page's title, meta description and canonical tag
Check robots.txt and sitemap.xml, and flag a broken one as missing
Pull Core Web Vitals from the public PageSpeed API
Report a failed fetch as a failure instead of guessing a result
Run an offline demo before pointing it at your own site
modules.needs: Your site URL. A PageSpeed API key only for Core Web Vitals

groups.label: Audio, video and images
groups.blurb: Production work that used to mean an editor, a freelancer, or an afternoon.

modules.name: descript
modules.label: Descript
modules.tagline: Imports media, tracks jobs and edits projects in your own Descript account.
modules.description: Descript connects to your own account with your API key. It imports media from a URL or a local file into a new project, tracks the job, lists and inspects projects, and fetches transcripts from anything you have published. The AI editor instruction applies straight to the live project with no preview step, so be clear about which project you mean.
canDo: Import media from a URL into a new project
Import a local file through your own cloudflared tunnel
Check the state, progress and result of a running job
List projects and inspect their compositions
Fetch a published transcript as text, VTT or raw JSON
Send a plain language edit instruction to Descript's own AI editor
modules.needs: Your own Descript API key, plus cloudflared for local file imports

modules.name: elevenlabs
modules.label: ElevenLabs
modules.tagline: Turn a script into narration on your own ElevenLabs account.
modules.description: It lists your voices, resolves a voice by name, checks your remaining balance, and writes generated speech to a file you name. Long scripts get split into safe chunks. Generation runs straight away and reports the character cost, so ask for the plan first if you only want the estimate. It stops if the text is bigger than the credits you have left.
canDo: List the voices on your account and resolve one by name
Generate speech from text into an audio file you name
Narrate a long script by splitting it into safe chunks
Estimate the character cost before you spend anything
Check how many speech credits you have left
modules.needs: Your own ElevenLabs API key and credit balance

modules.name: flow
modules.label: Flow
modules.tagline: Generate a short video clip from a written description.
modules.description: It submits video generation jobs to your own configured model and hands you back a job reference. Video takes minutes, so nothing comes back finished: you check the status when you want it. Every submission spends money on your account immediately, with no confirmation step in between, and reports the cost when the provider gives one.
canDo: Submit a video job from a written description
Include a reference image and an aspect ratio with the request
Check whether a submitted job has finished
Report what a submission cost when the provider returns a figure
Confirm your video key is configured before you try to generate
modules.needs: Your own Gemini API key with billing enabled

modules.name: open-generative-ai
modules.label: Generative Media Connector
modules.tagline: Sends image and video requests to your own muapi, fal.ai, or Replicate account.
modules.description: This is plumbing, not a creative tool. It forwards a request to whichever generative media account you have connected, muapi.ai, fal.ai, or Replicate, and hands back exactly what that provider returned. Every call previews for free first and runs only when you confirm, because most of them cost money. It never quietly routes a call to a provider you did not ask for.
canDo: See which providers you have connected and which one is active
Check a provider is reachable without spending anything
Preview a request before any money is spent
Send the request to your chosen provider once you confirm
Report back any cost or credit figure the provider returned
modules.needs: Your own API key for muapi.ai, fal.ai, or Replicate

modules.name: image-upscaler
modules.label: Image Upscaler
modules.tagline: Upscale PNGs on your own machine, with the originals left untouched.
modules.description: It finds the PNGs in a folder you choose and runs your local Upscayl binary over them, writing results into a separate output directory. Originals are never overwritten, and neither are existing outputs. Nothing leaves the machine: no upload, no account, no API call.
canDo: Upscale a single PNG into a separate output directory
Upscale every PNG in a folder you choose
Preview the filenames, count, scale and model before processing
Refuse to overwrite an original or an existing output
Check that the upscaler binary and model folder are configured
modules.needs: A local Upscayl binary and model folder on your machine

modules.name: kling
modules.label: Kling
modules.tagline: Make video from a description, a photo, or an audio track for lip sync.
modules.description: It submits jobs to your own Kling account: text to video, a still photo animated into a clip, or a video lip synced to an audio file. Jobs run in the background, so you get a task ID back rather than a finished video, and you check on it when you like. Every generation is billed to your own account, and each result names the model and price band it charged.
canDo: Submit a video job from a written description
Animate a still image into a video clip
Lip sync an existing video to an audio track
Check whether a submitted job is ready yet
See the model and price band charged for each job
modules.needs: Your own Kling access key and secret key

modules.name: video-editor
modules.label: Video Editor
modules.tagline: Trim, resize, and caption video on your own machine, with no keys.
modules.description: It drives ffmpeg on your machine for the mechanical jobs: cut a clip, resize it for Reels, TikTok, YouTube, or square, pull the audio out, and burn in a caption file you already have. It never edits your original and refuses to overwrite an existing output. No network calls, no credentials, and no AI generation of any kind.
canDo: Trim a clip between a start and an end point
Resize a video for Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube, or square
Extract the audio track as a WAV file
Burn an existing SRT or VTT caption file into a video
Inspect a file's duration, resolution, codec, and size
Check whether ffmpeg and caption burning are available here
modules.needs: ffmpeg installed on your machine, nothing else

modules.name: whisk
modules.label: Whisk
modules.tagline: Blend a subject, a scene, and a style into one new image.
modules.description: You give it three reference images: what the picture is of, where it is set, and how it should look. It describes each one, composes them into a single prompt, and generates a new image into a folder you choose. Describing and generating both call a paid provider on your account and run straight away, and every result names the model and the cost.
canDo: Describe a reference image before you use it
Combine subject, scene, and style references into one new image
Save generated images to an output folder you choose
Report the model used and the cost of each call
Check whether an image provider key is configured
modules.needs: Your own OpenAI or HuggingFace API key

groups.label: Research and the web
groups.blurb: Finding out what is true before you act on it.

modules.name: gemini-search
modules.label: Gemini Search
modules.tagline: Answer questions with current web results and the sources behind them.
modules.description: It calls Gemini's own Google Search grounding to answer a question with current results and the sources that produced them. A second mode runs a two-step pass for a deeper look at a topic. It only reads: no scraping, no crawling, no logins, no forms, and it says so plainly when a call comes back with no sources.
canDo: Run a grounded web search and return the sources with the answer
Run a two-step research pass on a topic
Report an unsourced or failed call rather than answering from memory
Check whether your API key is configured
modules.needs: Your own Gemini API key

modules.name: webfetch
modules.label: Web Fetch
modules.tagline: Fetches, screenshots and extracts web pages, politely and by the rules.
modules.description: Web Fetch takes a page request and picks the cheapest tool that can answer it, from a plain static fetch up to a full browser. It checks robots.txt and waits between requests to the same domain. Media downloads that would need your browser cookies require an explicit authorisation, so it is not a way around a login or a paywall.
canDo: Fetch and read a page, checking robots.txt first
Take a full page screenshot
Save a page as a PDF
Extract text or attributes by CSS selector
Download public or explicitly authorised media
Wait between repeat requests to the same domain
modules.needs: Nothing for basic fetching. Playwright for screenshots and PDFs, yt-dlp for media

modules.name: enrichment
modules.label: Website Enrichment
modules.tagline: Builds a short, sourced profile of a public website from its own pages.
modules.description: Give it one URL and it returns the title, description, canonical URL, an og:image reference, and any contact links the site already prints in public. It checks up to three of that same site's contact and about pages, never another domain. It does not guess an email address, write to a CRM, or keep anything after the response.
canDo: Profile a public website from a single URL you supply
Pull the title, description and canonical URL
Collect emails and phone numbers the page already publishes
Check the site's own contact, about and team pages
See exactly which pages were read for each result
Switch the extra page scan off and read only the URL you gave
modules.needs: A public website URL. No account or key

groups.label: Documents, contracts and files
groups.blurb: Paperwork read, checked, signed and filed.

modules.name: lawyer
modules.label: Contract Structure Check
modules.tagline: A mechanical structure check over a contract, before a lawyer reads it.
modules.description: It reads the text of a document and reports which of eighteen standard sections it can find, every blank never filled in, every cross reference pointing at a clause number no heading uses, every term defined and then never used again, and every sentence over sixty words. It is not legal advice, it rates no risk, and it makes no judgement about whether a term is fair or right for you.
canDo: Report which of eighteen standard sections a document contains
Find every blank, placeholder and TBD marker, with its line
Catch cross references pointing at a clause number no heading uses
Flag terms defined in quotation marks and then never used again
List every sentence over sixty words
Outline a services, non-disclosure, supply, licence or employment document
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline

modules.name: docuseal
modules.label: DocuSeal
modules.tagline: Send documents for signature and chase the people who have not signed.
modules.description: It sends a PDF out to the signers you name, tracks who has completed it and who has not, reminds the ones still outstanding, and downloads the finished document. Every call goes to your own DocuSeal instance with your own API key. Nothing reaches a signer until you confirm the send, and it never signs on anyone behalf.
canDo: Send a PDF out for signature to the signers you name
Check who has signed and who is still pending
Remind only the signers who still need to act
List documents still awaiting signature
Download a completed, fully signed document
modules.needs: Your own DocuSeal URL and API key

modules.name: dropbox
modules.label: Dropbox
modules.tagline: Moves documents in your own Dropbox, and sends them out for signature.
modules.description: This connects to your own Dropbox through OAuth. It moves files where you want them, clears out the conflicted copies Dropbox leaves behind, and sends a document out for e-signature through Dropbox Sign. The cleanup lists the exact files first and deletes nothing without your confirmation. A signature request waits for your approval before it goes anywhere.
canDo: Move a document to a different folder
List the conflicted copies before anything is removed
Delete those conflicted copies once you confirm
Send a document out for e-signature, after you approve it
Check that your Dropbox connection is working
modules.needs: Your own Dropbox account, connected by OAuth

groups.label: Security
groups.blurb: The stack that watches your business while you are not looking.

modules.name: git-guardian
modules.label: Git Guardian
modules.tagline: Tells you which project folders hold work that is not backed up yet.
modules.description: Git Guardian checks the repositories you point it at and reports uncommitted work, missing remotes, unpushed commits and unfinished merges. Everything but one action is read only. The save action shows you what would be committed and whether it would be pushed, and does nothing until you type SAVE. It never force pushes or rewrites history.
canDo: Check repository health across every folder you list
Rank repositories by how much work is at risk of being lost
Find branches that have gone quiet or fallen behind their remote
Preview what a checkpoint commit would include and where it would go
Commit and push that checkpoint once you confirm with SAVE
modules.needs: Nothing beyond the Git setup already on your machine

modules.name: guard-dog
modules.label: Guard-dog
modules.tagline: Check a package for known trouble before it gets into your project.
modules.description: It looks up npm and PyPI packages against public vulnerability feeds, download reputation, GitHub advisories, and suspicious code patterns, then returns one of three verdicts: silent, whine, or bark. The useful baseline needs no keys at all. An install only goes ahead once you confirm it, and a bark verdict blocks the install outright.
canDo: Scan a single npm or PyPI package before you install it
Scan every dependency listed in a project's package file
Install a package only after the scan clears and you confirm
Block an install outright on a dangerous verdict
Check which optional security integrations are switched on
modules.needs: Nothing for the baseline. VirusTotal and Telegram alerts need your own keys.

modules.name: threat-intelligence
modules.label: Threat Intelligence
modules.tagline: Sorts a pile of security findings into a ranked list you can act on.
modules.description: Give it your findings and it deduplicates them where identifiers match, scores impact, exploit evidence, exposure and patch state separately, and explains every ranking including what it is unsure about. It can pull a single CVE from the National Vulnerability Database, or a GitHub advisory with your own token. It recommends a next action and an owner, never an automatic production change.
canDo: Assess a supplied set of security findings
Deduplicate items only where the identifiers match
Rank work by impact, exploit evidence, exposure and patch state
Fetch a CVE record from the National Vulnerability Database
Look up a GitHub security advisory by ID or by package
Write a local Markdown review report
modules.needs: Nothing for offline triage. A GitHub token for advisory lookups

groups.label: Websites, code and infrastructure
groups.blurb: The plumbing under your own web presence, owned by you.

modules.name: domain-search
modules.label: Domain Search
modules.tagline: Finds candidate domain names and checks whether they are actually free.
modules.description: Domain Search suggests clean, pronounceable names for a brand, then checks availability against public RDAP and DNS, or against Cloudflare Registrar when you add your own credentials. It reads only. It cannot register, buy, renew or transfer anything, so the purchase still happens with your registrar of choice.
canDo: Suggest candidate domain names for a brand or keyword
Check one domain against public RDAP and DNS records
Get registrar grade status and price through your Cloudflare account
See how strong each availability signal really is
Run the suggestion demo offline before adding any credentials
modules.needs: Nothing for the basic checks. A Cloudflare account ID and API token for registrar checks

modules.name: git-manager
modules.label: Git Manager
modules.tagline: Backs up work in progress, and commits to your branch only when you confirm.
modules.description: Git Manager keeps your unsaved work safe. A snapshot parks the current state on its own checkpoint reference without touching your working files, your index, or any branch, so it can run at any moment. Turning that into a real commit on your branch previews first and waits for the exact confirmation word. It never pushes, resets, rebases, or rewrites history.
canDo: Snapshot uncommitted work without touching your branch
Show what has changed since the last commit, and by how much
List branches and recap recent commits
Run a health check on the repository
Commit a checkpoint onto your branch after you confirm
modules.needs: The path to your own repository. No account, no credentials.

modules.name: porkbun
modules.label: Porkbun
modules.tagline: Reads and edits DNS for the domains you already own at Porkbun.
modules.description: This connects to your Porkbun account with your own API keys. Lookups are free and instant: what you own, what a domain costs, which nameservers it uses, what its DNS records say. Changing a record, a forward, or a nameserver returns a preview of exactly what would change and waits for you to confirm. It does not buy, renew, or transfer domains.
canDo: Check whether a domain is available and what it costs
List the domains you own and their DNS records
See the nameservers and URL forwards on a domain
Create, edit, or delete a DNS record after you confirm
Add or remove a URL forward once you approve it
Fetch the SSL bundle for one of your domains
modules.needs: Your Porkbun API key and secret key

modules.name: shlink
modules.label: Shlink
modules.tagline: Turns a long URL into a short link on your own Shlink server.
modules.description: This makes short links on a server you run, so the links sit on your own domain and nobody else holds the click data. It logs into your VPS over SSH and calls a helper script there. Until the host, key, and script are set up, it tells you exactly what is missing instead of failing quietly, and there is a smoke mode for trying it with no server at all.
canDo: Turn a long URL into a short link on your own domain
Set the slug yourself, for an event or a campaign
Run it in smoke mode with nothing connected
Check whether your host, SSH key, and helper script are configured
modules.needs: A VPS you can SSH into, an SSH key, and your short-link domain

modules.name: supabase
modules.label: Supabase
modules.tagline: Reads and edits rows in your own Supabase tables, inside set limits.
modules.description: A bounded operator for your Supabase project. Reads name their columns and carry a row limit. Inserts, updates, and upserts run when you call them, and an update or delete with no filter is refused before anything is sent. A delete always previews: it shows the matching rows and the count, and removing them takes a second call carrying that count. No raw SQL, no schema changes.
canDo: Read rows from a table with named columns and a row limit
Insert a row, or upsert one that may already exist
Update the rows that match a filter you supply
Preview exactly which rows a delete would remove
Delete them on a second call carrying the confirmed count
Check that your project URL and key are set up
modules.needs: Your Supabase project URL and key

modules.name: vercel
modules.label: Vercel
modules.tagline: Shows what is deployed on Vercel, and runs a deploy when you ask.
modules.description: This reads your Vercel account so a release stops being a hunt across four screens: projects, recent deployments, the state of one release, its build logs, and which domains point where. A deploy runs the moment you call it, so use the plan flag first to see the folder and environment it would use. Production needs its own flag, set on purpose.
canDo: List your projects and recent deployments
Check the state of a single deployment
Read the build logs when a release fails
See which domains are connected
Preview a deploy before it runs
Deploy, with production behind its own explicit flag
modules.needs: Your own Vercel token

groups.label: Home and personal
groups.blurb: The rest of your life, on the same machine, off by default.

modules.name: bee
modules.label: Bee
modules.tagline: Read back what your Bee wearable already captured, on your own account.
modules.description: A thin wrapper around your own Bee CLI. It checks whether the device is connected, summarises what today captured, and searches back through the conversations, facts and todos the device already synced. It records nothing itself, and it will not authenticate for you or export your data anywhere outside your own sync folder.
canDo: Check whether your Bee wearable is connected
Summarise what the device captured today
Search past conversations, facts and todos by keyword
Report an empty result plainly instead of inventing a memory
modules.needs: Your own Bee account and CLI, plus a sync directory you choose

modules.name: amazon-shopping
modules.label: Shopping Planner
modules.tagline: Turns a shopping list into a research plan before you spend anything.
modules.description: Give it your list and it returns a research plan for each item, plus a comparison checklist for anything you are weighing up. It runs offline, with no connection to Amazon or any other retailer: no live prices, no cart, no checkout. The searching and the buying still happen in your own browser, on your own account.
canDo: Turn a list of items into a per item research plan
Set a quantity and buying guidance for each item
Get a pre-purchase comparison checklist for one item
Compare price per unit, ratings, seller trust and return window
Save the plan locally to work through later
modules.needs: Nothing, works offline

modules.name: smart-home
modules.label: Smart Home
modules.tagline: Controls your own Hue lights and Tuya devices by outcome, not by command.
modules.description: This talks to a Philips Hue bridge on your local network and to your own Tuya account. Ask for cosy, focus, or movie, and it runs the Hue scene you made under that name, or falls back to a set brightness and warmth. Rooms go on, off, brighter, dimmer, or warmer. Tuya devices switch on and off only. These run straight away, with no confirmation step.
canDo: List your lights, rooms, scenes, and Tuya devices
Check what is still on, across the house or in one room
Set the mood for a film, a call, or reading
Turn a room on, off, brighter, dimmer, or warmer
Turn every light and device off in one go
modules.needs: A paired Hue bridge on your network, plus Tuya cloud keys if you use Tuya

modules.name: spotify
modules.label: Spotify
modules.tagline: Search, play, and build playlists on your own Spotify account.
modules.description: It connects to a Spotify account you authorised yourself, through your own developer app and token. It searches the catalogue, tells you what is playing, lists your devices and playlists, and controls playback. Creating a playlist runs straight away and reports back the name, how many tracks went in, and any track it could not find.
canDo: Search the catalogue for a track, album, or playlist
Show what is playing right now
Play, pause, skip, and change the volume
List the devices that can play music
Create a playlist from tracks you name, and list the ones you have
Check whether your connection is still authorised
modules.needs: Your own Spotify client ID and access token
